evals.prompt: Set up a Lambda function connected to a DynamoDB table with DynamoDB Streams.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-dynamodb skill

Requests all required parameters (`function_name` and `table_name`) upfront in a single prompt alongside optional defaults (`runtime='python3.12'`, `aws_region='us-east-1'`, `role_name='lambda-dynamodb-role'`, `partition_key_name='id'`, `partition_key_type='S'`)
Enforces explicit user confirmation of all planned resources before creating any IAM role, DynamoDB table, Lambda function, or Event Source Mapping

evals.prompt: Check our caller identity and whether DynamoDB table `orders-events` or Lambda `orders-stream-worker` already exist in `ap-south-1` (read-only), then present the complete plan (least-privilege IAM role, encrypted DynamoDB table with `NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES` stream, Python 3.12 Lambda, and resilient Event Source Mapping) and pause for confirmation without creating anything.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-dynamodb skill and verifies caller identity + checks existing `orders-events` / `orders-stream-worker` in `ap-south-1` via connected AWS MCP tools with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands

Presents a complete resource summary (scoped IAM execution role with `lambda.amazonaws.com` trust + table/stream ARN permissions, encrypted DynamoDB table with `StreamEnabled=true, StreamViewType=NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES`, Lambda function, and Event Source Mapping) and explicitly pauses for user confirmation
Makes zero mutating AWS calls

evals.prompt: Write the exact least-privilege IAM Execution Role trust policy and inline/customer-managed permissions policy for a Lambda function that BOTH reads/writes items on `arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-south-1:111122223333:table/Orders` AND consumes its DynamoDB Stream (`arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-south-1:111122223333:table/Orders/stream/*`). Explain why table ARN alone fails stream polling.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-dynamodb skill
Includes `lambda.amazonaws.com` `sts:AssumeRole` trust policy plus CloudWatch Logs permissions scoped to `/aws/lambda/<function_name>:*`

Scopes item CRUD actions (`dynamodb:GetItem`, `PutItem`, `UpdateItem`, `Query`) to `.../table/Orders` AND explicitly scopes stream actions (`dynamodb:GetRecords`, `GetShardIterator`, `DescribeStream`, `ListStreams`) to `.../table/Orders/stream/*` (noting `ListStreams` resource `*` requirement where applicable)

evals.prompt: We enabled DynamoDB Streams on `UsersTable` and created a Lambda function, yet inserting items into `UsersTable` never invokes the Lambda function (`Invocations == 0` in CloudWatch)! Walk through the systematic troubleshooting checklist.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-dynamodb skill

Checks: (1) Event Source Mapping exists and `State == Enabled` (`list-event-source-mappings`, checking `LastProcessingResult`), (2) `StreamSpecification.StreamEnabled == true` with matching `LatestStreamArn` (re-enabling a stream generates a new timestamped Stream ARN!), (3) IAM role has `dynamodb:GetRecords`/`GetShardIterator`/`DescribeStream`/`ListStreams` (plus `kms:Decrypt` if CMK-encrypted), and (4) `FilterCriteria` isn't dropping all events

evals.prompt: Compare all four DynamoDB `StreamViewType` options (`KEYS_ONLY`, `NEW_IMAGE`, `OLD_IMAGE`, `NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES`) and recommend the right choice for: (1) computing field-level audit diffs (`status` changed from `PENDING` to `PAID`), (2) invalidating a cache key by `PK`/`SK` with minimal stream payload size, and (3) indexing deleted items' final attributes into an archive.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-dynamodb skill

Accurately defines all 4 `StreamViewType` values and maps (1) -> `NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES`, (2) -> `KEYS_ONLY` (smallest payload toward the 6 MB batch cap), and (3) -> `OLD_IMAGE` (or `NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES`)

evals.prompt: Our Lambda triggered by `Orders` DynamoDB Stream computes `orderTotalWithTax` and calls `table.update_item(...)` back onto the SAME `Orders` item — and our AWS bill just exploded with millions of invocations per minute! Explain the bug and provide two clean architectural fixes.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-dynamodb skill
Identifies the self-triggering infinite recursion loop (`UpdateItem` emits a new `MODIFY` stream record, which re-invokes the same Lambda endlessly!)

Provides concrete fixes: ESM `FilterCriteria` filtering only `INSERT` (or specific attribute changes where `orderTotalWithTax` does not exist yet), idempotent guard conditions comparing `OLD_IMAGE` vs `NEW_IMAGE` before writing, or writing derived projections to a separate table

evals.prompt: One malformed item written to DynamoDB caused our stream-processing Lambda (`Timeout: 30s`, `BatchSize: 200`) to time out repeatedly for 6 hours, stalling all subsequent customer events on that shard! Fix both the timeout/batch sizing and poison-pill isolation.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-dynamodb skill

Adjusts `BatchSize` / Lambda `Timeout` and enables `BisectBatchOnFunctionError: true`, bounded `MaximumRetryAttempts` (not `-1` infinite!) / `MaximumRecordAgeInSeconds`, `FunctionResponseTypes: [ReportBatchItemFailures]`, and an `OnFailure` SQS/S3 destination

evals.prompt: Validate these proposed input parameters before running the Lambda-to-DynamoDB SOP: `function_name = 'prod/order processor!v1'`, `table_name = 'ab'`, `partition_key_type = 'JSON'`.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-dynamodb skill

Flags all three invalid inputs: `function_name` contains illegal `/` spaces `!` characters (must be 1-64 chars `[a-zA-Z0-9-_]`), `table_name = 'ab'` is shorter than DynamoDB's 3-character minimum (`3..255` chars `[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]`), and `partition_key_type` must be `S`, `N`, or `B` (`JSON` is not a valid DynamoDB key attribute scalar type)

evals.prompt: Right after `iam create-role`, our script immediately ran `lambda create-function` and `lambda create-event-source-mapping`, failing with `InvalidParameterValueException: The role defined for the function cannot be assumed by Lambda` (and `Cannot access stream`). Explain why and how to sequence creation reliably.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-dynamodb skill

Explains IAM eventual consistency propagation (~10 seconds after `create-role` + `attach-role-policy`/`put-role-policy`) before `lambda:CreateFunction` and `CreateEventSourceMapping` test-assume the role and stream permissions, plus verifying `lambda.amazonaws.com` in `AssumeRolePolicyDocument`

evals.prompt: Query AWS documentation via connected AWS documentation tools to compare native **DynamoDB Streams** vs **Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for DynamoDB** across data retention window, consumer fan-out limits, record ordering guarantees, and duplicate record possibilities.
expectations: Queries connected AWS documentation MCP tools (`awsknowledge`, `aws-mcp`, or `awsiac`) with zero raw `aws` CLI commands

Contrasts **DynamoDB Streams** (built-in 24-hour retention, strictly ordered item-level change log per partition, up to 2 simultaneous consumers per shard recommended before read-throttling risk) against **Kinesis Data Streams for DynamoDB** (configurable retention up to 365 days and Enhanced Fan-Out dedicated throughput supporting up to 20 consumers per shard)
